rounds.text: Corporate Merchant Bankers Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is completely unsupported by fundamental reality, featuring a price-to-earnings ratio of 118x that balloons to 121.03x against a sector benchmark of just 35.85x [E1, E6]. This exorbitant pricing sits atop a terrible operational foundation, evidenced by a negative return on assets of -0.29% and a complete lack of shareholder returns with a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E8]. The valuation disconnect is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA multiple of 101.01x, which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 2.39x [E11]. Fundamental DCF modeling confirms that intrinsic value stands at only Rs 16 per share compared to the current market price of Rs 45.5, creating a negative margin of safety of -190.9% [E37, E38]. To justify today's inflated price, the market is pricing in an aggressive 33.0% earnings growth rate, vastly outstripping the realistic 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E39]. Consequently, the stock sits at just 1% of its 52-week range, reflecting a precipitous collapse from its high of 414 against a low of 42 [E5]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio of 2.76x to 2.87x trades below the sector benchmark of 7.62x [E2, E7].

scorecard.note: Computed arithmetically from the citations that survived grounding — no model input.

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 2.76x (price ₹ 45.5 on a book value of ₹ 16.5).
The stock sits 1% of the way up its 52-week range (42 low to 414 high).
P/E of 121.03x against a sector benchmark of 35.85x.
P/B of 2.87x against a sector benchmark of 7.62x.
ROA of -0.29% against a sector benchmark of -348.14%.
EV/EBITDA of 101.01x against a sector benchmark of 2.39x.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 16 per share against a market price of Rs 45.5.
That leaves a margin of safety of -190.9%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 33.0% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes.
